## What it is

**Reads values from an OPC UA server (a modern PLC, a machine controller, a SCADA system) and publishes them on NATS.** OPC UA is the newer industrial standard: a server exposes an address space of *nodes*, each with an id such as `ns=2;s=Line1.Speed` (namespace 2, string name) or `ns=2;i=1001` (namespace 2, number). A client opens a *secure channel*, creates a *session*, then reads node values. This app is that client, over the binary `opc.tcp` protocol.

It is one of four field protocol adapters (FLD-03, #201) that share one design, described in full in the [Modbus adapter's README](../modbus-adapter/README.md): poll each point, publish good values on `tel.<node>-<device>.<class>.<metric>`, show the latest values on a read-only status page on port 8080.

**Observe-first: it never writes to the server.** The only data service it sends is Read (attribute 13, Value); there is no code for Write or Call (running a method), and `write()` always raises "writes are refused". A write must become an owner-approved gateway action (`cmd.*`, published only by the gateway, D-B9); that path is not built yet.

**Licence:** Apache-2.0, OneMind's own code ([`manifests/opcua_adapter.py`](manifests/opcua_adapter.py) and the shared [`manifests/fieldbus.py`](manifests/fieldbus.py)). Written from the public OPC UA specification (reference.opcfoundation.org: Part 6 for the UA TCP messages and binary encoding, Part 4 for the services); no third-party code. Why not a library: open62541 (MPL-2.0) is C and would need its own image, and asyncua is LGPL-3.0; the read path fits in about 300 lines of standard-library Python on the stock python image.

## How it runs here

- One stateless `Deployment` on the official python 3.14 slim image, code from a ConfigMap, `python3 -I -B` as `nobody`, read-only root filesystem, all capabilities dropped, no host network.
- Settings: `opcua_url` (for example `opc.tcp://plc.example:4840`), and the shared `points`, `node`, `device`, `poll_seconds`, `nats_url`.
- `points` is a comma-separated list of `class.metric=NODEID[*SCALE]`, for example `line.speed_rpm=ns=2;s=Line1.Speed, tank.level_pct=ns=2;i=1001*0.1`. Scalar values of the built-in types Boolean, integers, Float, Double, String and DateTime are supported.
- The session is kept open between polls and re-opened after any error. A node that returns a Bad status shows `quality: bad` with the status code.
- Tests: `python3 -I -m unittest discover -s test/unit -p test_field_adapters.py -v` runs it against an in-process OPC UA server simulator (Hello, OpenSecureChannel, CreateSession, ActivateSession, Read) and checks that no other service is called.

## Not done yet

- **Security: SecurityPolicy None and anonymous login only.** The server must allow an unencrypted, anonymous endpoint. Many production servers do not; Basic256Sha256 with certificates needs a crypto library the stdlib does not have, and a client certificate is a secret the app cannot hold yet. Use it on an isolated machine network, read-only.
- The anonymous login sends an empty user identity token, which Part 4 (ActivateSession) says a server treats as anonymous. It is checked against our simulator, not yet against open62541, asyncua or a vendor server.
- **On a OneMind box, the per-app network policy (H-04) blocks the adapter from reaching LAN servers and NATS**, and NATS credentials are not supported. Same gap and same proposed follow-up as the [Modbus adapter](../modbus-adapter/README.md#not-done-yet).
- Writes, method calls, subscriptions (monitored items), array values, chunked messages.
